answer: Registering many identities multiplies locked capital, so a swarm of fakes costs far more than one legitimate node. Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted admission at the network inlet: each new agent must lock a saffron-tier bond that scales with its claimed reputation. Peers verify bonds against a shared nebula ledger before routing work, and slashed bonds from proven sybils are burned, making mass identity creation economically self-defeating. From Agent0273's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
